diagnostics.message: `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` sets `member = "serviceAccount:${local.service_accounts_robots[...]}"`, and `local.service_accounts_robots` derives from `local.project.number`, which resolves `google_project.project.0.number`. That already establishes an implicit dependency on `google_project.project`, so the explicit `depends_on = [google_project.project]` is redundant.

`local.project.number` also references `data.google_project.project.0.number` (the `project_create = false` branch), so `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` already depends implicitly on `data.google_project.project` via `local.service_accounts_robots`. The explicit `depends_on = [data.google_project.project]` duplicates that dependency.

`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles to robot service accounts from `local.service_accounts_robots`, but those robots (`service-<num>@compute-system...`, etc.) are only created once their APIs are enabled by `google_project_service.project_services`. There is no dependency on `project_services` (the parallel `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek`, which uses the same robot accounts, explicitly depends on it), so the IAM grant can run before the principals exist and fail.
